bull_case: Alphabet still combines more than $155B of cash and marketable debt securities with very large OCF. Debt/equity financing funds an extraordinary growth buildout rather than operating losses, so survival risk remains low.
bear_case: The balance sheet has become materially more capital intensive: $707B of fixed or guaranteed commitments, large new debt issuance, mandatory convertibles and a $40B ATM create financing and dilution pressure if AI returns disappoint.
thesis: Alphabet's financial survival remains strong, but the company is no longer balance-sheet-light. Core operations generate ample cash and liquid assets still broadly cover debt, clearing structural external-capital dependence. The main penalty is commitments and dilution optionality: $707B of fixed/guaranteed commitments equal roughly 1.6x TTM revenue, while Q2 diluted shares rose about 0.9% YoY after new common/preferred issuance. That drives dilution/off-balance to 55 without creating a Hard Veto.

evidence.claim: At June 30, 2026 Alphabet held $55.9B cash and $99.5B marketable debt securities, while long-term debt was about $98.2B before the August $25B senior-note offering.
FY2025 operating cash flow was $164.7B and H1 2026 OCF was $84.9B, demonstrating very large internal funding capacity even though H1 capex reached $80.6B.
At June 30, 2026 expected future fixed or guaranteed commitments were $707.0B, the significant majority related to long-term technical-infrastructure supply agreements.

Q2 2026 diluted shares used in EPS were 12.309B versus 12.198B in Q2 2025, about +0.9% YoY; FY2025 diluted shares were 12.230B versus 12.447B in 2024 and 12.722B in 2023, so the multi-year trend before the 2026 financing was downward.
Alphabet issued $10B of common stock and $19B of mandatory convertible preferred stock in June 2026, established a $40B ATM with no sales as of June 30, and had no share repurchases in H1 2026.

counterevidence: H1 2026 capex of $80.6B consumed almost all H1 operating cash flow, reducing self-funded free-cash-flow headroom.
The $707B commitment stack is large relative to roughly $446B of trailing revenue and reduces flexibility if AI demand or pricing disappoints.
Mandatory convertibles and a still-unused $40B ATM create future dilution capacity even though current dilution is modest.
Debt issuance accelerated materially in 2026 and the August $25B notes increase gross leverage further.
unknowns: Exact cancellation and rescheduling flexibility of the $707B commitment stack by counterparty and year.
Maintenance versus growth share of AI infrastructure spending.
Post-August deployment of new debt proceeds and resulting quarter-end net liquidity.
falsifiers: Operating cash flow falls below mandatory infrastructure commitments and debt service for a sustained period.
ATM or other equity issuance becomes recurrent to fund ordinary operations rather than discretionary growth investment.
Diluted share growth exceeds 3% annually for multiple periods without corresponding per-share economic-value growth.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: The underlying business produces very large operating cash flow. 2026 financing supports an extraordinary discretionary AI infrastructure program rather than proving ordinary operations cannot self-fund.

Q2 diluted shares rose only about 0.9% YoY and the 2023-2025 diluted-share trend was downward. The long-duration and excessive-dilution elements are therefore not met despite mandatory convertibles and unused ATM capacity.

hard_veto_flags.veto: 파산 또는 영구손실 확률이 기대수익에 비해 지나치게 높음
hard_veto_flags.rationale: Large liquid assets and operating cash flow make insolvency or business-value extinction unlikely at the cutoff. Valuation drawdown and commitment risk are handled in scores, not double-counted as this veto.

key_kpis.name: OCF less capex
key_kpis.threshold: clear positive annual owner cash generation after the current buildout

key_kpis.name: Fixed commitments / revenue
key_kpis.threshold: fall materially from the current ~1.6x TTM revenue level

next_checks: Update debt, liquid assets and financing usage after Q3 2026.
Track whether the $40B ATM remains unused and how mandatory-convertible dilution evolves.
Recompute fixed commitments/TTM revenue and capex/OCF as AI infrastructure comes online.

subscores.rationale: Cash plus marketable debt securities exceed June long-term debt and OCF is very large. The score stays at the 75 strong-liquidity anchor rather than 90 because gross debt rose sharply in 2026 and another $25B was issued in August.

Core operations generate enough cash to survive a downturn without mandatory equity funding, but the exceptionally high capex/commitment load would force investment reprioritization under stress, preventing a 90.

Q2 diluted shares rose about 0.9% YoY, mapping the dilution axis to 55. Fixed/guaranteed commitments of $707B are roughly 1.6x estimated TTM revenue (~$446B), also mapping the off-balance axis to 55; the rubric takes the lower axis.

uncertainties.rationale: The post-August balance of cash versus debt depends on how financing proceeds were deployed.
Management's ability to cancel or defer long-term infrastructure commitments is only partly disclosed.
Mandatory preferred conversion and ATM capacity create dilution optionality even though current net dilution remains below monitor thresholds.

dilution_metrics.rationale: Q2 2026 diluted shares were about 0.9% above Q2 2025, while annual diluted shares declined from 12.722B in 2023 to 12.447B in 2024 and 12.230B in 2025. Current watch therefore remains normal despite preferred-conversion and ATM optionality.
